jp: 駅前[えきまえ]の観光[かんこう]案内所[あんないじょ]が閉[し]まっていたので、明日[あした]また{出[で]直[なお]す|cv-naosu}ことにした。
en: The tourist information office by the station was closed, so I decided to come back again tomorrow.
why: 出直す means to go out and come again later after a failed attempt; 直す gives the 'start over' sense.

jp: 切符[きっぷ]売[う]り場[ば]で違[ちが]う列[れつ]に並[なら]んでいたので、最後尾[さいこうび]に{並[なら]び直[なお]しました|cv-naosu}。
en: I had been in the wrong line at the ticket counter, so I got in line again at the back.
d: 並[なら]べ直[なお]しました
並[なら]び過[す]ぎました
並[なら]び切[き]りました
why: 並び直す is to line up again, the right reading when you were in the wrong queue.

jp: そのバスは終点[しゅうてん]の公園前[こうえんまえ]で{折[お]り返[かえ]して|cv-naosu}、また駅[えき]へ向[む]かいます。
en: That bus turns around at the terminus in front of the park and heads back to the station.
why: 折り返す means to turn back along the same route, as buses do at the end of a line.

jp: 朝[あさ]は雨[あめ]だったが、昼[ひる]から天気[てんき]が{持[も]ち直[なお]して|cv-naosu}、予定[よてい]どおり観光[かんこう]ができた。
en: It rained in the morning, but the weather recovered from midday and we could sightsee as planned.
why: 持ち直す is intransitive 'recover, pick up again', used for weather or health.

jp: 道[みち]に迷[まよ]って不安[ふあん]になったが、気[き]を{取[と]り直[なお]して|cv-naosu}もう一度[いちど]地図[ちず]を見[み]た。
en: I got lost and felt uneasy, but I pulled myself together and looked at the map again.
why: 気を取り直す is the fixed phrase for recovering one's spirits and trying again.

jp: 靴[くつ]ひもがほどけたので、駅[えき]のベンチで{結[むす]び直[なお]した|cv-naosu}。
en: My shoelace had come undone, so I tied it again on a bench at the station.
why: 結び直す is to tie again; the lace came undone, so it needs to be retied.
